info.name: Financial App API
info.description: Complete API collection for Financial App - Health, Auth, Dashboard, Users, Categories, Transactions, Recurring Expenses, Payment Methods, Credit Cards, Notifications, and Budgets

request.description: Check the health status of the API server.
Login to get JWT token. The token will be automatically saved to environment variable 'auth_token'.
Logout the authenticated user. Requires a valid JWT token. The token and user_id will be automatically removed from environment variables upon successful logout.

Get complete dashboard data for the authenticated user. Returns financial summary (totalBalance, totalIncome, totalExpenses), recent transactions (last 10), and upcoming payments (next 10 active recurring expenses). All calculations are performed server-side.
Create a new user. Password must be at least 8 characters long.
Get all users in the system.
Get a specific user by ID.
Update a user. All fields (username, name, phone, email) are optional, but at least one field must be provided.
Delete a user by ID.

Create a new expense category. Type must be either 'income' or 'expense'. Save the category ID for use in transactions. The category type must match the transaction type (expense categories for EXPENSE transactions, income categories for INCOME transactions).

Create a new income category. Type must be either 'income' or 'expense'. Save the category ID for use in transactions. The category type must match the transaction type (expense categories for EXPENSE transactions, income categories for INCOME transactions).
Get all categories for the authenticated user. Optionally filter by type using the 'type' query parameter (income or expense).
Get all income categories for the authenticated user. The 'type' query parameter filters categories by type (income or expense).
Get all expense categories for the authenticated user. The 'type' query parameter filters categories by type (income or expense).
Get a specific category by ID.
Update a category. All fields (name, description, type) are optional, but at least one field must be provided. Type must be either 'income' or 'expense'.
Delete a category.
Create a manual transaction (not from recurring expense). Type can be 'INCOME' or 'EXPENSE'.
Process a payment from a recurring expense. This creates a transaction and updates the next payment date.

query.description: Filter by type: INCOME or EXPENSE

request.description: Get transaction history with optional filters. All query parameters are optional. Use 'type' parameter to filter by EXPENSE or INCOME.

query.description: Filter by type: INCOME or EXPENSE

request.description: Get all expense transactions for the authenticated user. Use type=EXPENSE to filter expenses only.

query.description: Filter by type: INCOME or EXPENSE

request.description: Get all income transactions for the authenticated user. Use type=INCOME to filter income only.
Get all transactions for the authenticated user without filters.

Update an INCOME transaction. Only INCOME transactions can be updated. All fields (amount, description, date, categoryId, paymentMethodId) are optional, but at least one field must be provided. Payment method is optional for INCOME transactions.
Delete a transaction by ID.
Create a new recurring expense. Frequency can be: WEEKLY, MONTHLY, or YEARLY. payDay is the day of the month (1-31).
Get all recurring expenses for the authenticated user.
Update a recurring expense. You can update any field: name, amount, currency, categoryId, paymentMethodId, frequency, payDay, startDate, nextPaymentDate, isActive.
Delete a recurring expense by ID.
Create a credit card payment method. card_number (required): Last 4 digits of the credit card (exactly 4 digits). cut_off_day (1-31): Day when statement closes. payment_day (1-31): Payment due date.
Create a bank account payment method. account_number must be exactly 4 digits. account_type can be 'SAVINGS' or 'CHECKING'.
Create a cash payment method. amount (required): Current cash amount (must be a positive number).
Get all payment methods for the authenticated user.

Update a credit card payment method. All fields (name, type, currency, details) are optional, but at least one field must be provided. If updating details without type, they will be merged with existing details. For credit cards, details can include: card_number (last 4 digits, required when changing type to CREDIT_CARD), cut_off_day (1-31), payment_day (1-31), credit_limit, current_balance.

Update a bank account payment method. All fields (name, type, currency, details) are optional, but at least one field must be provided. If updating details without type, they will be merged with existing details. For bank accounts, details can include: bank_name, account_number (exactly 4 digits), account_type (SAVINGS or CHECKING).

Update a cash payment method. All fields (name, type, currency, details) are optional, but at least one field must be provided. If updating details without type, they will be merged with existing details. For cash, details can include: amount (current cash amount, required when changing type to CASH).

Update only specific fields of a payment method. You can update just the name, currency, or specific details fields. If updating details without providing type, the details will be merged with existing details based on the current payment method type.

Calculate payment due date for credit card transactions. Returns null for non-credit card payment methods. Business logic: If transaction is before cut_off_day → payment due on payment_day of current month. If transaction is on/after cut_off_day → payment due on payment_day of next month.
Delete a payment method by ID.
Get all credit cards for the authenticated user with summary info (name, last 4 digits, credit limit, current balance, cut-off day, payment day).
Get full detail for a single credit card, including all fields and current balance information.

Returns the last 12 billing period statements for a credit card. Each statement includes totals, dates, and a summary. The first statement's periodStart will be automatically saved to the 'period_start' environment variable.

variable.description: ISO 8601 date string for the start of the billing period (e.g. 2024-01-15)

request.description: Returns the detailed view for a single billing period, including individual transactions and a category breakdown. The periodStart must be a valid ISO 8601 date string.

Registers a credit card payment from a bank account. Atomically creates an EXPENSE transaction and reduces the card's current balance. Fields: sourceAccountId (bank account payment method ID), amount (positive number), date (ISO 8601), billingPeriodStart (ISO 8601), billingPeriodEnd (ISO 8601, must be after billingPeriodStart). Returns the created transaction.
Returns the full payment history for a specific credit card, listing all payments made against this card.

Register an Expo push token for the authenticated user. The token will be added to the user's expoPushTokens array. Duplicate tokens are automatically prevented using MongoDB's $addToSet operation. Requires authentication via JWT token.

query.description: Maximum number of notifications to return (default: 20)
Number of notifications to skip for pagination (default: 0)

request.description: Get paginated notifications for the authenticated user. Notifications are ordered by createdAt descending (newest first). Both limit and offset query parameters are optional. Returns a paginated response with notifications array, total count, limit, and offset. The first notification ID will be automatically saved to the 'notification_id' environment variable.
Get notifications without pagination parameters. Uses default values (limit: 20, offset: 0). Notifications are ordered by createdAt descending (newest first).
Mark a notification as read. Validates that the notification belongs to the authenticated user. Returns the updated notification with isRead set to true. Requires authentication via JWT token.

Get the count of unread notifications for the authenticated user. Returns a simple object with the count property. Useful for displaying a badge with the number of unread notifications. Requires authentication via JWT token.

Create a new budget for the authenticated user. Fields: name (required, max 100 chars), amount (required, positive number), currency (required, 3 chars e.g. USD), period (required: WEEKLY, MONTHLY, or YEARLY), categoryId (optional, null for general budgets), startDate (optional, ISO date), rollover (optional, default false), alertThresholds (optional, array of numbers 1-100, default [80, 100]). The budget ID will be automatically saved to the 'budget_id' environment variable.

Create a general budget without a category. When categoryId is omitted or null, the budget tracks all expenses regardless of category. This example uses rollover=true and custom alert thresholds at 50%, 80%, and 100%.
Get all budgets for the authenticated user. Supports optional query parameters: isActive (boolean, filter by active status) and includeExpired (boolean, include expired budgets).

query.description: Filter by active status (true or false)

request.description: Get only active budgets for the authenticated user. Use isActive=true to filter active budgets, isActive=false to filter deactivated budgets.

query.description: Include budgets that have passed their end date (true or false)

request.description: Get all budgets including expired ones. By default expired budgets are excluded; use includeExpired=true to include them.
Get active budgets sorted by consumption percentage descending. Used for the dashboard widget to show budgets that are closest to their limit first.
Get expired or inactive budgets for the authenticated user. Useful for reviewing past budget performance.
Get a specific budget by ID for the authenticated user.
Update mutable fields of an existing budget. Only name, amount, alertThresholds, and rollover can be updated — period and categoryId are immutable after creation. At least one field must be provided.
Soft-delete (deactivate) a budget by setting isActive to false. The budget is not permanently removed and can still be viewed in the history endpoint.
